[04/11/25, 17:07:52] Arjun Karunakar Gim Sarc Senior: Hello Ma’am,
Thank you for your feedback.

We would like to clarify that, we specifically mentioned that the event was a collaboration among three entities and did not state that it was “organized by” us. This phrasing was chosen thoughtfully, as we felt it more accurately represented the partnership dynamics and the collective efforts involved.

Moreover, in a one-on-one conversation, our S.A.R.C. member was informed by you that there were only five registrations and that, since it was a “S.A.R.C. event,” it was S.A.R.C.’s responsibility to increase those numbers. Our communication was therefore aligned with that understanding.

We would also like to highlight that the phrase “supported by S.A.R.C.” is not contextually accurate, as traditionally, a larger or official entity supports a smaller one. Therefore, the Alumni Office, being in an institutional capacity, can support; whereas S.A.R.C., as a student volunteer body, can only organize or collaborate.

It is, however, disheartening to see divisions being drawn and our efforts going unacknowledged, such as during the vote of thanks at past events. The Student Alumni Relations Cell functions under the guidance of the Director and the Chair, with the shared objective of strengthening Alumni relations and advancing the institute’s larger vision. As a volunteer body, S.A.R.C. does not work for monetary benefit or because it falls within a job description, our efforts stem purely from commitment and a sense of belonging to the institution.
We hope this provides clarity on our intent and approach, which were consistent with both precedent and the information available to us at the time.
